UBS Global Research 2 March 2026 Advanced Micro Devices Inc Takeaways From Semis Bus Tour Summary Thoughts We emerged more confident in revenue upside for C2027 as the company is now suggesting there could be a third GW-scale customer beyond the deals it has struck with OpenAI and META. While we can't be sure who this is, MSFT seems to us the most likely. Regarding investor concerns that the warrant structure and 10% equity stakes for META/OpenAI will now become pre-requisites for GW-scale engagement, AMD pushed back aggressively and indicated that it considers these to be unique deals targeted for LLM model builders because they are controlling so much of the ecosystem. AMD also views this structure as accretive longer term and a vehicle to dramatically accelerate its share gains in the broader accelerator market. AMD was very bullish on the CPU business and now sees upside to the LT financial model's 18% market CAGR both from units and ASPs. Overall, we emerge confident in our $310 PT and Buy rating, though we do believe AMD is probably more of a 2H:26 story as MI450 shipments related to the OpenAI deal commence, followed shortly thereafter by META shipments. Jean Hu (CFO) Liz Stine (Sr. Director, IR) Prabh Gowrisankaran (Director, IR) META has long been a customer of the AMD GPU business, so the 6GW announcement this week is not entirely incremental but was not accounted for in full during the Analyst Day. AMD notes it may accelerate the timeline to the announced $20 EPS target (or potentially increase it above $20).  Similar to OAI, AMD views META as one of the top five LLM developers, and a strong ramp with those should help AMD accelerate market share gains. AMD suggested warrants were part of the deal structure for key LLM builders, but AMD will be very selective and not offer such arrangements to every customer. LT OpM of the GPU business is closer to 35% (vs 25%), and AMD views these first two large deals as increasing scale to drive long-term economic value. The META warrants, like the OAI warrants, have additional technical conditions requiring the customer to prepare its software stack and not just take shipments.  OAI shipments are expected slightly ahead of META, but with no unique tape-out META should also start to ramp in C2H26.  AMD is also now suggesting there could be a 3rd GW-scale customer in addition to OAI/META, but it may not make a public announcement based on the customer's preference.  AMD suggested that powered shell availability might be a risk to the ramp to 3GW of shipments in C2027. The company is confident in its work with the supply chain to prepare for the MI450 ramp.
 AMD highlighted that system-level design includes networking components. AMD has a competitive DPU product with Pensando but relies on partners for switching products. AMD was an investor in Celestial AI with right of first refusal which it declined to exercise at the time of the MRVL acquisition due to lack of product synergies.
Server CPU market growth has been in excess of AMD's expectations. The November Analyst Day estimates were developed in summer 2025, and since then demand signals have continued to strengthen. AMD now sees potential upside to its $60B C2030 market size and 18% 5yr CAGR driven by both units and ASPs.
AMD now sees CPU market benefiting from unit demand driven by AI and traditional applications, aided by an upward ASP trend. On the ASP side in particular, AMD traditionally thought of core count increase offsetting downward trend in ASP per core - but now AMD expects ASP per core to remain flattish.
AMD's recent multi-year strategic partnership with Nutanix highlights the strength of CPU demand for agentic use cases and accelerates AMD's momentum in the enterprise server CPU side of the market (incremental to its strong position with hyperscalers). According to AMD, Nutanix did not need the cash investment, but AMD buying $150MM of Nutanix stock helps AMD share in the potential upside.
 AMD viewed 1 Q as "quite strong" for PC market, but the company expects momentum to slow down in 2Q with memory pricing headwinds and thinks that 2Q and 2H PC revenues will likely be sub-seasonal. Ultimately, for the year AMD thinks units may decline MSD.
On the margins side, AMD reiterated 55-58% LT GM target, but also noted that it is willing to trade GM for higher market share. Ultimately, AMD thinks GPU margins will normalize, but the company pointed to server CPU as a case study, noting that EPYC Rome (2nd gen) margins were meaningfully lower than current server CPU margins. Like server CPU, AMD expects data center GPUs to have a strong margin profile over the long term.
 AMD acknowledged higher-than-expected C2025 OpEx due to accelerated development of three GPU programs at once (with significant tape-out costs). Going forward, AMD thinks it should start seeing OpEx leverage in C2026 and accelerating in C2027+ as GPU revenues gain scale.

Company Description Founded in 1969, Advanced Micro Devices is a Santa Clara, CA-based company specializing in advanced x86-based microprocessors and chipsets for client desktop and notebook PCs and cloud/data center servers, as well as complex graphics processors (GPUs) and chipsets that drive workstation and PC graphics and advanced deep learning/AI platforms. The company also sells semi-custom solutions, development services, and intellectual property licenses. Valuation Method and Risk Statement We value AMD based on a NTM P/E methodology. Upside risks to our AMD thesis include higher-than-anticipated penetration into cloud/data center servers and better traction in AI. Downside risks include margin pressure in the form of aggressive price competition from Intel and an inability to effectively shift production to TSMC in a timely manner.
